bug_semantics: Flux Operator Web UI OIDC login accepts a valid token, evaluates impersonation CEL, and then builds a Kubernetes client from the resulting username/groups with no non-empty check. Default expressions `has(claims.email) ? claims.email : ''` and `has(claims.groups) ? claims.groups : []` yield empty string and empty slice when those claims are absent (custom CEL can do the same). client-go then sets rest.ImpersonationConfig{UserName:"", Groups:[]} and omits impersonation headers, so subsequent Web UI API calls run as the flux-operator service account instead of the authenticated user.
flaw_origin: First written in the original Web UI authentication commit eba38678 (PR #519 member, not the later claims.go extract). That commit added the empty-fallback CEL defaults, the OIDC claims extractor that returned username/groups with only CEL-eval errors checked, and newUserClient which always copied those values into rest.ImpersonationConfig. The same commit already rejected empty username+groups for Anonymous config validation, but never applied an equivalent runtime check to the OIDC evaluation path. Later package moves/refactors (936c575, d85f2b0, 01779b5, e197b2a) relocated the same mechanism; they did not introduce it.
